topic.source_contract: Playing-field protection, Sport England consultation and planning evidence

facts.policy: object unless one or more of five exceptions is met
facts.guard: policy response is not the local planning authority decision

facts.definition: playing-field site contains at least one playing pitch; pitch and run-off area at least 0.2 hectares
facts.guard: service availability and consultation are not planning outcomes

sources.publisher: Department for Culture, Media and Sport

facts.role: protect playing fields through statutory-consultee function
facts.guard: consultation duty does not transfer decision-making authority
strategy or calculator is not site permission or delivered capacity

facts.proposal: possible changes to Sport England statutory-consultee role
facts.guard: consultation proposal is not enacted current law

scope_guards: A playing field, playing pitch, open space and sports facility are related but distinct concepts.
The statutory playing-pitch definition and 0.2 hectare threshold require exact current use and geometry.
Sport England consultation and objection do not replace the local planning authority decision.
The five policy exceptions require proposal-specific evidence and are not automatic approvals.
A Playing Pitch Strategy or needs assessment is strategic evidence and not a site permission or delivery record.
Replacement provision, community-use agreements and conditions require exact legal and implementation evidence.
Proposed statutory-consultee reforms are not applied before enactment and commencement.
No score or promotion is written without exact field history, use, geometry, consultation, exception, legal agreement and planning evidence.
